title: Radiation-tolerant structural alloys for advanced reactors
bottleneck: Fast-neutron fluxes in advanced reactors cause void swelling, embrittlement, and creep that can ruin structural steels within years. Oxide-dispersion-strengthened steels and high-entropy alloys show better tolerance in ion-irradiation tests, but ion beams do not fully replicate neutron damage, and real fast-neutron test reactors are scarce and oversubscribed. Qualifying any new alloy takes a decade of irradiation campaigns.
why_it_blocks: Advanced reactors promise safer, cheaper nuclear power, but their business cases assume components last the plant lifetime. Without qualified radiation-tolerant materials, designers must derate performance or accept costly replacements, eroding the economic case.
current_state: Ferritic-martensitic steels are the near-term reference, with ODS variants in qualification pipelines. New test reactors coming online this decade should accelerate data collection, but no advanced-reactor structural alloy is fully qualified yet.
